originalTitle: China has banned hidden retractable car door handles. How are they dangerous – and what will Australia do?
summary: The handles, which were popularised by Elon Musk’s Tesla EVs, have a record of failing and trapping passengers inside burning vehicles during deadly accidents
content: They used to be a novelty in Australia: the futuristic, flush-mounted car door handles favoured by Elon Musk’s Telsas. However while the design – popularised with the Tesla Model S in 2012 and since adopted by other manufacturers – might look sleek, it may not be great in an emergency. After several deadly high-profile accidents involving different makes and models, in which power failings saw people trapped inside the vehicle, China has announced a world-first ban on hidden or retractable electric car door handles. But with less than six months to go before the ban is implemented, and domestic demand for electric vehicles booming, experts say it’s time for Australia to adopt the same precautions. What is changing? While hidden door handles are used by car manufacturers around the world, they are particularly popular in China. As of April 2026, about 60% of the country’s 100 bestselling “new-energy vehicles” – EVs, hybrids or fuel cell-powered cars – had them, according to the China Daily. From 1 January 2027, all new cars sold in China will be required to have a mechanical release on both the inside and outside of every door except the boot, according to regulations announced in February by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology. Under the changes, on the outside of every door there must be a recessed space measuring at least 6cm by 2cm by 2.5cm for a hand to grasp the handle and manually open the door. On the inside, there must be signs showing occupants how to manually open the door. The ban will apply to both press-to-release hidden handles and electrical pop-out or retractable handles, Bloomsberg reported. The idea is that people will be able to open a car from the inside or outside in an emergency, even if the handle has lost power. Some manufacturers whose new models have already been approved for sale have been given a two-year grace period to update their designs. Tesla had already flagged design changes. In September last year, the company’s chief of design, Franz von Holzhausen, told Bloomberg it was looking to combine the electronic and manual door-release mechanisms, to make them more intuitive for occupants in “a panic situation”. What does this mean for Australia? Australia imports all its cars, and there has been a recent influx of Chinese-made EVs due to their relative affordability. “About 60% of all new vehicles sold in Australia are made in China but that’s because they’re very good at making cars now, and Australians love a bargain,” says Chris Jones from the Australian Electric Vehicle Association (AEVA). Every car in the Top 10 EVs sold in May this year was primarily built in China, with manufacturers Tesla, Jaecoo, Geely, BYD and Zeekr behind the top models, according to Carsguide. Jones says the Chinese ban won’t extend to flush mounted door handles that can still be operated manually, which are the kind typically seen in Australia, so the ban may not apply to models currently popular in the country. However, Jones says it’s a good time to reconsider the Australian Design Rules – the national standards governing vehicle safety, anti-theft and emissions. “I think there is a perfectly reasonable case to mandate a manual mechanism on both inside and outside the vehicle for front and rear doors,” he says. “The Chinese government has recognised this flaw and the potential for disaster when extracting casualties from a crash, so are regulating accordingly.” What are the rules in Australia now? A spokesperson for the transport minister, Catherine King, says all road vehicles, including EVs, must have doors that can be opened without the use of tools. In practice, this means all car door must be operational by hand. Although vehicles are tested for this function after both side and frontal impact crashes, this only applies to the outdoor handles as “there is usually no way to test the internal door handle following a crash test” using a dummy. King’s spokesperson says the government has provided the independent safety assessor ANCAP with $16.3m in funding over 5 years to increase their door handle assessment as part of their Star Safety Rating Program. Carla Hoorweg, the ANCAP chief executive officer, says the Australian Design Rules haven’t kept up with technology and don’t prescribe enough detail. “That’s what we want to make sure the rules are really clear on – that there has to be a manual override from the inside and the outside,” she says. “It’s both, so that occupants can get out and so first responders can get into the vehicle. “The objective is reducing the risk of entrapment after a crash.” Guardian Australia has contacted Tesla for comment. Will cars banned in China be “dumped” in Australia? The issue made headlines again earlier this month after the peak body for car and truck dealers – the Australian Automotive Dealers’ Association – released a report warning of the “risk of stock dumping following China’s approach to EVs with flush door handles”. While cars rejected by the Chinese are unlikely to be literally “dumped” here – their steering wheels would be on the wrong side for Australian roads – Hoorweg says there is a risk that cars with less safe door handles could end up being sold here. “If there’s a lot of door handles floating around and they’re cheap because they can’t sell them in China, what are you going to do with them?” she says.
chineseTitle: 中国已禁止使用隐藏式可伸缩汽车门把手。它们有多危险——澳大利亚会做什么？
chineseSummary: 这些手柄因埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 的特斯拉电动汽车而广受欢迎，但在致命事故中曾出现过故障，并将乘客困在燃烧的车辆内。
chineseContent: 它们曾经在澳大利亚是一种新奇事物：埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 的特斯拉公司 (Telsas) 青睐的未来派嵌入式汽车门把手。然而，虽然这种设计在 2012 年随特斯拉 Model S 流行起来，后来被其他制造商采用，但虽然看起来很时尚，但在紧急情况下可能不太好。在发生了多起涉及不同品牌和型号的致命事故（其中有人被困在车内）之后，中国宣布在全球范围内首次禁止使用隐藏式或可伸缩电动汽车门把手。但距离禁令实施还有不到六个月的时间，而且国内对电动汽车的需求正在蓬勃发展，专家表示，澳大利亚是时候采取同样的预防措施了。什么正在改变？虽然隐藏式门把手被世界各地的汽车制造商使用，但它们在中国尤其受欢迎。据《中国日报》报道，截至 2026 年 4 月，中国 100 辆最畅销的“新能源汽车”（电动汽车、混合动力汽车或燃料电池汽车）中约 60% 拥有此类汽车。根据工业和信息化部今年 2 月发布的规定，自 2027 年 1 月 1 日起，所有在中国销售的新车将被要求在除行李箱外的每个车门的内侧和外侧安装机械解锁装置。修改后，每扇门的外侧必须有一个至少6厘米×2厘米×2.5厘米的凹陷空间，以便手抓住把手并手动打开门。在内部，必须有标志向居住者展示如何手动开门。据彭博社报道，该禁令将适用于按下释放的隐藏式手柄和电动弹出或可伸缩手柄。这个想法是，即使把手断电，人们也可以在紧急情况下从内部或外部打开汽车。部分厂家
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
